description: The bar chart illustrates the performance of various fine-tuning methods on the GLUE benchmark for two sizes of the RoBERTa model: base and large. The x-axis represents different fine-tuning methods, including Prefix, Adaptor, LoRA, BitFit, S1-model, S4-model, and S5-model. The y-axis measures the GLUE performance, with values ranging from approximately 84 to 89. The chart compares the performance of the base and large RoBERTa models across these methods. The base model generally shows lower performance than the large model, with the largest performance gap observed in the S5-model method. The S1-model and S4-model methods appear to have similar performance for both model sizes, while the Prefix and Adaptor methods show a significant performance difference between the two model sizes. The BitFit method has the highest performance for the large model, while the base model's performance is slightly lower but still competitive. The chart also includes two random baselines for comparison: S_0-model, where all designs are randomly selected for RoBERTa, and S_3-model, where strategies are randomly assigned to different layers while following other design choices learned from T5 models.
